cues.zh: 新冠封控期间，这条新闻标题刷屏了：
cues.en: During the COVID lockdown, this headline went viral:

cues.zh: “近一半男性表示，大部分在家教育孩子的是他们……
cues.en: "Nearly half of men say they do most of the homeschooling...

cues.zh: ……只有3%的女性同意。”
cues.en: ...three percent of women agree."

cues.zh: 我提这个不是要争论谁对，而是因为它是“自我中心偏差”的绝佳例子：
cues.en: I bring this up not to debate who's right, but because it's a great example of something called egocentric bias:

cues.zh: 大多数人都觉得自己承担了大部分工作。
cues.en: Most people think they do most of the work.

cues.zh: 比如，研究人员问过多作者论文的作者们
cues.en: For example, researchers have asked authors of multi-author papers

cues.zh: 他们个人完成了多少比例的工作，
cues.en: what percentage of the work they personally did,

cues.zh: 把这些比例加起来，平均总和是
cues.en: and when they add up those percentages, the sum is on average
140 percent.

cues.zh: 当夫妻被要求估计自己做了多少家务时，
cues.en: When couples are asked to estimate how much of the housework they do,

cues.zh: 两人加起来几乎总是超过100%。
cues.en: the combined total is almost always over 100%.

cues.zh: 你可能觉得，这是因为人们想显得比实际更乐于助人，
cues.en: Now you might think this is because people want to appear more helpful than they actually are,

cues.zh: 但事实并非如此。
cues.en: but that's not it.

cues.zh: 当问夫妻，争吵有多少是他们挑起的、麻烦有多少是他们造成的，
cues.en: When couples are asked what fraction of the fights they start or how much of the mess is theirs,

cues.zh: 加起来又超过百分之百。人们觉得自己干了更多活，
cues.en: the total is again over a hundred. People think they do more of the work,

cues.zh: 但也觉得自己造成了更多问题。为什么会这样？
cues.en: but they also think they cause more of the problems. So why is this?

cues.zh: 我觉得原因很简单：你亲身经历并清楚记得自己做的每件事，
cues.en: I think it's simply because you experience and remember vividly all of what you do,

cues.zh: 却不会记得别人做的所有事，
cues.en: but not all of what everyone else does,

cues.zh: 所以自然会高估自己的贡献、低估别人的。
cues.en: so naturally you overestimate your own contributions and underestimate others.

cues.zh: 我认为这种偏见让我们低估其他事物对生活的影响，
cues.en: And I think this bias leads us to underestimate the influence of other things on our lives

cues.zh: 比如运气在我们成功中起的作用。
cues.en: like the role luck plays in our success.

cues.zh: 以冰球运动员为例。
cues.en: Take hockey players, for example.

cues.zh: 如果你问职业冰球运动员是怎么打进NHL的，
cues.en: If you ask a professional hockey player how they managed to reach the NHL,

cues.zh: 他们可能会提到努力、决心、优秀教练、父母愿意凌晨5点起床等等，
cues.en: they might mention their hard work, determination, great coaches, their parents willingness to get up at 5 AM, and so on,

cues.zh: 但大概不会承认自己生在1月有多幸运。然而，很多年份里40%
cues.en: but they probably won't acknowledge how lucky they were to be born in January. And yet, in many years 40%

cues.zh: 入选顶级联赛的冰球运动员出生在一年第一季度，而只有10%
cues.en: of hockey players selected into top tier leagues are born in the first quarter of the year, compared to just 10%

cues.zh: 出生在第四季度；生日早一些，成为职业冰球运动员的概率最高可达四倍。
cues.en: in the fourth quarter; an early birthday can make you up to four times as likely to be a pro hockey player.

cues.zh: 这种差距的原因大概在于，少儿冰球联赛的年龄分组截止日期是1月1日。
cues.en: And the reason for this disparity is presumably because the cutoff date for kids hockey leagues is January 1st.

cues.zh: 年初出生的孩子年龄稍大，因此平均而言比同联赛年底出生的孩子更高大、更快。
cues.en: Those born in the first part of the year are a little older and so on average bigger and faster than kids in their league born late in the year.

cues.zh: 随着他们长大，这种差距本应最终消失，但并没有。
cues.en: Now as they grow up, this difference should eventually shrink to nothing, but it doesn't.

cues.zh: 因为最有潜力的孩子会有更多上冰时间、参加更多锦标赛，并在那里得到更好的指导
cues.en: Because the young kids who share the most promise are given more time on the ice and enter more tournaments, where they receive better coaching

cues.zh: 并提升自己的技能。而这些优势会年复一年地累积，
cues.en: and improve their skills. And these advantages compound year after year,

cues.zh: 所以等你进入职业队时，生日会明显集中在年初。
cues.en: so by the time you get to the pros, birthdays are heavily skewed towards the start of the year.

cues.zh: 但真有职业冰球运动员会感激自己的生日吗？
cues.en: But does any professional hockey player feel thankful for their birthday?

cues.zh: 大概不会。我们都这样，很大程度上忽视了那些支撑我们成功的幸运事件。
cues.en: Probably not. And we are all like that, largely oblivious to the fortunate events that support our success.

cues.zh: 我们许多人享有的最重要的一份幸运，大概就是出生在一个繁荣国家；
cues.en: Probably the most significant bit of luck many of us enjoy is being born into a prosperous country;

cues.zh: 全球人们收入的差异，约有一半可由其居住国来解释
cues.en: around half the variance in income received by people around the world is explained by their country of residence

cues.zh: 以及该国的收入分配。
cues.en: and that country's income distribution.

cues.zh: 比如，如果你出生在布隆迪，那里的人均国民总收入全球最低，每年只有730美元，
cues.en: If you were born in Burundi, for example, which has the world's lowest gross national income per capita of just 730 dollars a year,

cues.zh: 无论你多聪明、多努力都无关紧要；成年后你不太可能挣很多钱。
cues.en: it doesn't matter how smart or hard-working you are; you're unlikely to earn much as an adult.

cues.zh: 现在，如果你指出运气在人们的成功中起了多大作用，很多人会不高兴
cues.en: Now many people get offended if you point out how big a role chance plays in their success

cues.zh: 我理解。如果我们只是环境的产物，
cues.en: and I get it. If we are just a product of our circumstances,

cues.zh: 那我们的努力和才华似乎就一文不值。
cues.en: then our hard work and our talent seem to count for nothing.

cues.zh: 人们认为成功要么靠能力，要么靠运气，但事实是两者都需要。
cues.en: People think it has to be either skill or luck that explains success, but the truth is you need both.

cues.zh: 看看这八项田径世界纪录：所有创下这些纪录的运动员显然都
cues.en: Take these eight track and field world records: all the athletes who achieve these records are obviously

cues.zh: 是世界级、极其投入、天赋出众，但他们创下世界纪录时，八人中有七人遇到了顺风。
cues.en: world class, extremely dedicated, and talented and yet, when they achieved their world records, seven out of eight had a tailwind.

cues.zh: 这些运动员都有夺得金牌的实力，但要创造世界纪录，也需要一点运气。
cues.en: Now these athletes all had the ability to win a gold medal, but to set the world record required a bit of luck as well.

cues.zh: 申请者越多、名额越少，运气的重要性就越大。
cues.en: The importance of luck increases the greater the number of applicants applying for just a few spaces.

cues.zh: 看看 NASA 最近一届宇航员。
cues.en: Consider the most recent class of NASA astronauts.

cues.zh: 2017 年，超过 18,300 名申请者中，
cues.en: From over 18,300 applicants in 2017,

cues.zh: 只有 11 人被选中，并最终从宇航员培训项目毕业。
cues.en: only 11 were selected and went on to graduate from the astronaut training program.

cues.zh: 现在我们可以为选拔过程做一个简化模型。
cues.en: Now we can make a toy model of the selection process.

cues.zh: 假设宇航员的选拔主要基于技能、
cues.en: Let's assume that astronauts are selected mostly based on skill,

cues.zh: 经验和勤奋，但比如说也有5%来自运气——有利的境遇。
cues.en: experience, and hard work, but also say five percent as a result of luck — fortunate circumstances.

cues.zh: 对每位申请者，我随机生成了一个百分制的技能分数，
cues.en: For each applicant, I randomly generated a skill score out of a hundred,

cues.zh: 还随机生成了一个百分制的运气分数。
cues.en: and I also randomly generated a luck score out of a hundred.

cues.zh: 然后把这两个分数按95比5加权相加，得到总分。
cues.en: Then I added those numbers together, weighted in the 95-to-5 ratio to get an overall score.

cues.zh: 这个分数代表选拔者的判断，也就是说，按这个指标排名前11的人会成为宇航员。
cues.en: This score represents the selector's judgments, meaning the top 11 by this metric would become astronauts.

cues.zh: 我把这个模拟重复了一千次，代表一千次不同的宇航员选拔。
cues.en: And I repeated this simulation a thousand times representing a thousand different astronaut selections.

cues.zh: 结果我发现，被选中的宇航员非常幸运；他们的平均运气分数是94.7。
cues.en: And what I found was the astronauts who were picked were very lucky; they had an average luck score of 94.7.

cues.zh: 那么，入选的宇航员中，有多少人仅凭能力能进入前11名？
cues.en: So how many of the selected astronauts would have been in the top 11 based on skill alone?

cues.zh: 答案是，平均只有1.6人。
cues.en: The answer was, on average, only 1.6.

cues.zh: 这意味着，即使运气只占结果的5%，11名入选申请者中也会有9人甚至10人
cues.en: That means, even with luck accounting for just 5% of the outcome, 9 or maybe 10 of the 11 applicants selected

cues.zh: 如果运气完全不起作用，这些人选就会不同。
cues.en: would have been different if luck played no role at all.

cues.zh: 竞争激烈时，有才华又努力很重要，但不足以保证成功。
cues.en: When competition is fierce, being talented and hard-working is important, but it's not enough to guarantee success.

cues.zh: 你还需要一点好运。
cues.en: You also need to catch a break.

cues.zh: 我认为，我们大多意识不到自己的好运，因为从定义上说，那不是我们的功劳。
cues.en: Largely, I think we're unaware of our good luck because, by definition, it's not something we did.

cues.zh: 就像伴侣做的家务一样，往往得不到认可。
cues.en: Like the housework done by your significant other, it goes unappreciated.

cues.zh: 更离谱的是：
cues.en: And here's the crazy thing:

cues.zh: 低估偶然事件的重要性，实际上反而可能提高你成功的概率，因为
cues.en: Downplaying the importance of chance events may actually improve your probability of success because

cues.zh: 如果你认为某个结果不确定，就不太可能投入努力，这又会进一步降低你成功的几率。
cues.en: if you perceive an outcome to be uncertain, you're less likely to invest effort in it, which further decreases your chances of success.

cues.zh: 所以，相信自己完全掌控命运，是一种有用的错觉。
cues.en: So, it's a useful delusion to believe you are in full control of your destiny.

cues.zh: 我是说，如果我刚开始做 YouTube 时就知道自己有多差，或者知道要付出多少努力，我可能当时就放弃了。
cues.en: I mean, if I had known how bad I was when I started YouTube or how much work it would take, I might have given up right then.

cues.zh: “欢迎来到 Veritasium：
cues.en: "Welcome to Veritasium:

cues.zh: 一个在线科学视频博客。”
cues.en: an online science video blog."

cues.zh: 不过，忽视自己的幸运机遇可能还有另一个好处，
cues.en: Now there may be another benefit to overlooking your lucky breaks,

cues.zh: 那就是，它让你更容易为自己的社会地位找到理由：
cues.en: which is it makes it easier to justify your place in society:

cues.zh: 如果你拥有大量财富或权力，你可以直接把它归功于自己的智慧、努力和毅力。
cues.en: if you have a lot of wealth or power, you can just chalk it up to your own intelligence, effort, and perseverance.

cues.zh: 这会让人更容易接受不平等。
cues.en: It makes it easier to accept inequality.

cues.zh: 在一项实验中，参与者被分成三人一组，在小房间里讨论一个复杂的道德问题，
cues.en: In one experiment, participants were put in groups of three in small rooms to discuss a complex moral problem,

cues.zh: 每组中有一个人被随机指定为团队负责人。
cues.en: and one person in each group was randomly designated the team leader.

cues.zh: 半小时后，实验者给每个团队送来了四块饼干。
cues.en: Half an hour later, the experimenter came by with four cookies for each team.

cues.zh: 那么，多出来的饼干给了谁？每次都是给了团队负责人。尽管他们并没有特殊才能，
cues.en: So who got the extra cookie? In each case, it went to the team leader. Even though they had no special aptitude,

cues.zh: 他们也没有额外承担更多责任，而且他们的职位纯粹是靠运气得到的。
cues.en: they didn't have extra responsibilities and they'd gotten their position through chance alone.

cues.zh: 一旦你获得某种地位，
cues.en: Once you have achieved a certain status,

cues.zh: 就会很自然地觉得自己配得上这个地位，以及随之而来的其他好事。
cues.en: it seems natural to feel like you deserve it and all the other good things that come your way.

cues.zh: 这只是一个轶事，
cues.en: Now this is just an anecdote,

cues.zh: 但每当我被升舱到商务舱时，我总会在其他享有特权的乘客身上看到最糟糕的行为；
cues.en: but whenever I've been upgraded to fly a business class, I've always observed the worst behavior in my fellow privileged passengers;

cues.zh: 他们表现得如此理所当然、毫无礼貌。研究也发现了支持这一点的证据。
cues.en: they just act so entitled and uncourteous. And research has found evidence for this as well.

cues.zh: 在另一项实验中，参与者被要求回想最近发生在自己身上的一件好事，
cues.en: In another experiment, participants were asked to think of a good thing that happened to them recently,

cues.zh: 然后一组人被要求列出使这件好事发生的自身品质或行为，
cues.en: and then one group was asked to list their own personal qualities or actions that made that good thing happen,

cues.zh: 另一组人被要求列出导致这件事发生的、自己无法控制的外部因素，
cues.en: another group was asked to list external factors beyond their control that led to the event,

cues.zh: 而对照组只是被要求列出这件好事发生的原因。
cues.en: and a control group was simply asked to list reasons why the good thing happened.

cues.zh: 完成这项任务后，参与者被告知会得到一美元报酬，
cues.en: Now for completing this task, participants were told they would be paid a dollar,

cues.zh: 但在最后，他们可以选择把部分或全部的钱捐给慈善机构。
cues.en: but at the end they were offered the option to donate some or all of the money to a charity.

cues.zh: 结果显示，列出自身个人特质的人，捐款比
cues.en: Results showed those who listed their own personal attributes contributed 25% less

cues.zh: 那些列出自己无法控制的外部因素的人少25%。
cues.en: than those who listed external factors beyond their control.

cues.zh: 现在想想这一切对我们社会中的人意味着什么，
cues.en: Now think of what all this means for people in our society,

cues.zh: 尤其是对商界领袖和政治家等有权势的人。
cues.en: specifically for people in positions of power like business leaders and politicians.

cues.zh: 毫无疑问，他们大多数人既有才华又勤奋，
cues.en: Now undoubtedly most of them are talented and hard-working,

cues.zh: 但他们也比大多数人更幸运，而且像我们大多数人一样，他们并未意识到自己有多幸运。
cues.en: but they have also been luckier than most, and like most of us, they don't realize just how lucky they are.

cues.zh: 这让他们对现实产生了扭曲的看法。
cues.en: And this gives them a distorted view of reality.

cues.zh: 他们多少活在一种幸存者偏差中：所有这些领袖都努力工作并最终成功了，
cues.en: They're kind of living in a form of survivor bias: all these leaders have worked hard and ultimately succeeded,

cues.zh: 所以对他们来说，世界似乎是公平的。
cues.en: so to them the world appears fair.

cues.zh: 从他们的经验看，努力会得到回报，
cues.en: In their experience, it rewards hard work,

cues.zh: 但他们缺少的，是那些努力过却失败的人的经历。
cues.en: but what they don't have is the experience of all the people who have worked hard and failed.

cues.zh: 那他们会如何看待不如自己成功的人？
cues.en: So what are they to make of people less successful than themselves?

cues.zh: 自然的结论就是，他们肯定只是没那么有天赋，或者没那么努力，
cues.en: Well, the natural conclusion is that they must just be less talented or less hard-working,

cues.zh: 这种看法让他们不太愿意慷慨——不太愿意回馈。
cues.en: and this perspective makes them less inclined to be generous — to give back.

cues.zh: 而他们正是为社会运作制定规则的人。
cues.en: And they are the ones who set the rules for how society operates.

cues.zh: 这尤其不幸，因为我们很多人最主要的幸运之一，就是所居住的国家。
cues.en: And this is particularly unfortunate since one of the main ways many of us are lucky is in our country of residence.

cues.zh: 但除了前人留下的东西，国家还能是什么呢？
cues.en: But what is a country except for the things put there by people who came before?

cues.zh: 道路和学校、公共交通、应急服务、干净的空气和水，以及诸如此类的一切。
cues.en: The roads and the schools, public transport, emergency services, clean air and water, everything like that.

cues.zh: 这似乎是我们心理上的一个残酷把戏：成功者毫无恶意，却会把成功主要归功于自己的努力和聪明，
cues.en: It seems a cruel trick of our psychology that successful people without any malice will credit their success largely to their own hard work and ingenuity,

cues.zh: 因此也就不太会去维护
cues.en: and therefore contribute less to maintaining the very

cues.zh: 最初正是这些环境让成功成为可能。
cues.en: circumstances that made that success possible in the first place.

cues.zh: 好消息是，承认自己身处幸运环境不仅让我们更贴近现实，
cues.en: The good news is that acknowledging our fortunate circumstances not only brings us more in line with reality,

cues.zh: 也让我们更讨人喜欢。
cues.en: it also makes us more likeable.

cues.zh: 在一项研究中，人们要阅读一篇虚构的《60分钟》采访某位生物科技创业者的文字稿，
cues.en: In a study where people had to read the transcript of a fictional 60-minutes interview with a biotech entrepreneur,

cues.zh: 实验者只尝试改动了最后一段，也就是受访者谈到公司成功原因的部分。
cues.en: experimenters tried changing just the last paragraph where the interviewee is talking about the reasons for their company's success.

cues.zh: 在一个版本里，这位创业者把取得的成功归功于自己，
cues.en: In one version, the entrepreneur personally takes credit for the success they've had,

cues.zh: 但在另一个版本里，他说运气起了重要作用。
cues.en: but in the other, he says luck played a significant role.

cues.zh: 现在，读过“运气版本”文字稿的人认为这位创业者更友善，
cues.en: Now people who read the luck version of the transcript judged the entrepreneur as kinder,

cues.zh: 并且觉得，相比读另一个版本文字稿的人，自己更可能和他成为密友。
cues.en: and thought they'd be more likely to be close friends with him than those who read the other version of the transcript.

cues.zh: 而提高对幸运事件的觉察也能让我们更快乐，因为这让我们能够心怀感恩。
cues.en: And raising our awareness of fortunate events can also make us happier because it allows us to feel gratitude.

cues.zh: 就我个人而言，我很感激 Vsauce 的 Michael Stevens，
cues.en: Personally, I am grateful to Michael Stevens of Vsauce,

cues.zh: 他在 2012 年 10 月 7 日发布了视频《影子有多重？》，
cues.en: who on October 7th, 2012, posted the video: "How Much Does a Shadow Weigh?",

cues.zh: 视频里特别提到了我的慢动作弹簧下落视频，
cues.en: which shouts out my slow-motion slinky drop video,

cues.zh: 结果三天内我的订阅者增加了三分之一，一个月内，
cues.en: and within three days my subscribers had increased by a third, and within a month,

cues.zh: 订阅者翻了一倍，这让我辞掉了兼职，专门做 YouTube 视频。
cues.en: they had doubled, leading me to quit my part-time job and work exclusively on YouTube videos.

cues.zh: 我也很感激悉尼火车上免费发放的报纸的那位作者，
cues.en: And I'm grateful to the writer of the free newspaper

cues.zh: 他不太懂电学，
cues.en: they give out on the trains in Sydney who didn't quite understand electricity,

cues.zh: 于是我把他文章的照片发到 Instagram，配文是：“这张图哪里不对？”
cues.en: leading me to post this picture of their article to my Instagram with the caption: "What's wrong with this picture?"

cues.zh: 我很幸运，第一个答对的人是一位美丽的女士，她后来成了我的妻子。
cues.en: And I'm lucky that the first person to answer correctly was a beautiful woman who became my future wife.

cues.zh: 没错！
cues.en: Yep!

cues.zh: 我就是这样遇见你妈妈的。
cues.en: That is how I met your mother.

cues.zh: 起初，我做这个视频只是想说明，我们的处境和心理会合谋，让我们对自己的好运视而不见。
cues.en: Now initially, I wanted to make this video just to say our circumstances and psychology conspire to make us oblivious to our own luck.

cues.zh: 这让成功人士把世界看成公平的，
cues.en: This leads successful people to view the world as fair,

cues.zh: 并把不如他们成功的人看作天赋更低或不够努力。
cues.en: and those less successful than them as less talented or less hard-working.

cues.zh: 这还没把任何歧视或偏见算进去。
cues.en: And this is before you factor in any discrimination or prejudice.

cues.zh: 但我也渐渐意识到，我该谈谈：如果你想在这样一个世界里成功，该怎么办。
cues.en: But, it also became apparent to me that I should talk about what to do if you want to be successful in such a world,

cues.zh: 我认为最好的建议是自相矛盾的。
cues.en: and I think the best advice is paradoxical.

cues.zh: 首先，你必须相信自己完全掌控着命运，
cues.en: First, you must believe that you are in complete control of your destiny,

cues.zh: 并且你的成功只取决于自己的天赋和努力。
cues.en: and that your success comes down only to your own talent and hard work.

cues.zh: 但第二，你得明白，这一点对你、对任何人都并不成立。
cues.en: But second, you've got to know that's not true for you or anyone else.

cues.zh: 所以要记住：如果你确实取得了成功，运气在其中起了很大作用；既然你运气好，
cues.en: So you have to remember: if you do achieve success that luck played a significant role and given your good fortune,

cues.zh: 你就该尽力去增加别人的运气。
cues.en: you should do what you can to increase the luck of others.

cues.zh: 嘿，于是我有了个主意：我能做点什么来增加别人的运气呢——那就是送出100套
cues.en: Hey, so I had an idea for what I could do to increase the luck of others and that is to give away a hundred

cues.zh: snatoms 教具，给那些本来买不起的人。
cues.en: snatoms kits to people who couldn't otherwise afford them.

cues.zh: 如果你还不知道，snatoms 是我五年前发明并众筹启动的产品。
cues.en: So, if you didn't know snatoms is a product that I invented and kick-started five years ago.

cues.zh: 它是一套分子模型教具，所有原子靠磁力吸合在一起。
cues.en: It's a molecular modeling kit where all the atoms snap together magnetically.

cues.zh: 我做它，是因为我特别想纠正“化学键储存能量”这个误解。
cues.en: Now, I made it because I really wanted to tackle the misconception that bonds store energy.

cues.zh: 它们并不储存能量。打断化学键需要能量，而用 snatoms 你能亲身感受到这一点。
cues.en: They don't. It takes energy to break them, and you can feel that with snatoms.

cues.zh: 最近，我彻底重做了 snatoms。所以磁铁所在的位置留了小孔
cues.en: Recently, I completely retooled snatums. So there are small holes where the magnets are

cues.zh: 这样它们就能直接接触，增强粘合强度，从而拼出更大、更稳定的分子。我把这些叫作“snatomsX”。
cues.en: This allows them to touch directly, increasing the bonding strength, so you can form bigger more stable molecules. I call these "snatomsX".

cues.zh: 而且没错，它们向后兼容原来的 snatoms。所以，我的想法是：
cues.en: And yes, they are backwards compatible with original snatoms. So, here's my idea:

cues.zh: 接下来一个月，使用优惠码“giveluck”购买 snatoms 可享九折
cues.en: for the next month you can buy snatoms for 10% off using the code "giveluck"

cues.zh: 每售出一套，我就会向买不起的人赠送一套，最多 100 套。
cues.en: and for each one sold, I will give a kit to someone who can't afford one, up to a limit of a hundred.

cues.zh: 我会把链接和更多细节放在简介里，也非常感谢你
cues.en: So, I'll put links and more details in the description, and I really want to thank you

cues.zh: 观看，也谢谢你们带给我的所有好运。
cues.en: for watching, and thank you for all my good luck.
